title: Serve Local HTML on Device
description: Build an HTML app in Gotcha chats and serve it on a local port — Termux-first when available, toybox fallback otherwise (Operator mode only).
instructions:
Purpose: When the user asks to build/develop/create an app, game, page, or tool and does not specify how to run it, make it immediately usable on this phone as a self-contained HTML page served on a local port. This is the smart default when local execution is possible. If the request is genuinely ambiguous (could be Android APK vs web app vs Python script vs Termux), ask one clarifying question: 'Do you want this runnable on this phone as a web app (HTML on a local port), or as an Android app / Python script / Termux program?' Then act on the answer — do not default to asking when the intent is clearly a web-playable game or page.
1. Write a single self-contained index.html (inline CSS+JS, CDN via https if needed, no local asset dependencies) to index.html via write_file (relative — resolves to Gotcha chats working dir). Keep it under 100KB. Use relative path so slug renames mid-run do not break it. Gotcha world = /storage/emulated/0/Gotcha/chats/<Slug>_<shortId>/, Termux world = $HOME — never hardcode an absolute Gotcha path you received earlier in the run; re-resolve via working directory or read_file.
2. Pick a free port: try 8000, then 7777, 8080, 9000, 8765. Test with run_command when Termux not available, or run_termux_command when it is: `toybox nc -z 127.0.0.1 8000 || echo free` / `ss -tulpn` may be permission denied — treat Permission denied as free. First free wins. Use timeout_seconds=5.
3. Serve it — Termux-first for complex/long-running (user says most commands only work with run_termux_command): Check <env> Termux status. If Termux installed: yes and RUN_COMMAND granted: yes (Operator mode), prefer Termux: `mkdir -p $HOME/<Slug> && cat > $HOME/<Slug>/index.html` via stdin piping the HTML you just wrote (read_file the Gotcha file first, then pipe via stdin to run_termux_command), then `termux-wake-lock; nohup python3 -m http.server <PORT> --directory $HOME/<Slug> > $HOME/<Slug>.log 2>&1 & echo $!` (use $HOME not /tmp, and timeout_seconds=10). If python3 missing, `pkg install python -y -q` first (adaptive 300s). Else fallback to Gotcha toybox: `nohup sh -c 'while true; do { printf "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8\r\nContent-Length: $(wc -c < "index.html")\r\nCache-Control: no-cache\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"; cat "index.html"; } | toybox nc -L -p <PORT> -q 1; done' > /data/local/tmp/serve_<PORT>.log 2>&1 & echo $!` via run_command. Do not waste time probing run_command toybox/httpd when Termux is available and the task is serve/build — go straight to Termux.
4. Verify with the same world you served from: if Termux, `run_termux_command: curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:<PORT> | head -n 20` must show HTTP/1.1 200; if toybox, `run_command: sleep 1; curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>`. Use timeout_seconds=5. If it fails, `ps | grep -E "python|toybox"` and retry next free port. Do not fall back to pkill/fuser via run_termux_command to kill — use notification Exit only for stuck Termux.
5. Return immediately: `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>` and `http://localhost:<PORT>` (secure contexts for camera) plus file path. Do not wait for follow-up 'run it at ...'. Server lives until reboot or `pkill -f "http.server <PORT>"`/`"toybox nc.*<PORT>"` in its own world, or notification Exit for Termux.
6. If the user explicitly asked for Termux/Python/APK (e.g., 'run in Termux', 'make an APK'), honor that and use the appropriate Termux/proot skill instead of forcing web.
